walkers.name: sorn

born.strike: this is the station with the frightening name and the best hand on the road, and the three traditions disagree so completely that the disagreement is the reading. china calls it 虛 — the void, emptiness. the arabs looked at the same star and named it saʿd al-suʿūd, the luck of lucks — the luckiest star in the entire sky, and the name survives today: astronomers still call it sadalsuud. india named this sky śatabhiṣā, which means the hundred healers, and gave it an emblem of an empty circle, under varuṇa — god of oaths, hidden law, and deep water. a void. the greatest luck there is. a hundred physicians around an empty ring. put them together and you get something true: an opening is not a wound. your hunger is to heal the thing nobody could name — the undiagnosed, the unspoken, the problem everyone had learned to work around. the cost is the circle's own shape. you make room for other people's illness by keeping yourself open, and an opening does not close on command. you are extremely good at holding space and notably worse at being held.
born.facing: you enter and something in the room opens. people say things to you they have not said to anyone, often within the first conversation, and are sometimes embarrassed afterward. you are read as safe and slightly bottomless.

card.text: counts two, its right counts less

walkers.name: nefa
walkers.in: nefa cuts the ice, where there is ice. tonight there is nothing to cut and she is standing with the saw down, and does not seem to mind.

walkers.name: brann
walkers.in: brann fishes. through the ice, when there is ice; tonight through nothing at all. he has caught nothing and is not surprised.

walkers.name: oda
walkers.in: oda draws the blood off. the jar is at her hip and it is empty, which is how a physician likes a jar.

walkers.name: tam
walkers.in: tam sets bones. nothing is broken here. he is holding the splints anyway, because a physician who puts them down is not a physician.

walkers.name: hesh
walkers.in: hesh carries water. two pails on a yoke, both empty, both light, and he walks as if they were full.

walkers.name: sil
walkers.in: sil bleeds the fever out. there is no fever. she has let everything go that could be let go, and it went.

walkers.name: the old physician
walkers.in: the old physician's bag is closed. there is nothing left in it to give and nothing left out here to give it to.

walkers.name: the hundredth
walkers.in: the hundredth physician is the one who healed by leaving. you cannot quite see them.

arabia.name: Saʿd al-Akhbiya
arabia.meaning: "Luck of the Tents / of Hidden Things"

match.test: the traditions describe the same thing

claim: a tent, a rooftop, and a god who stands on one foot. three names for a shelter and the single upright holding it up.
synthesis: saʿd al-akhbiya is the luck of the tents — and of hidden things; china's 危 wēi is the rooftop; and india's aja ekapāda, the one-footed, is read as a pillar of fire, a thing that stands by having exactly one point of contact with the ground. the flag reads STRONG.
election: protection and hiding — what is inside the tent is safe, and every source recorded it that way. agrippa and picatrix also mark these degrees for sieges and binding, hostile flags kept on the history shelf.
archetype: a light here builds cover and lives under it. the four stars form a small tent shape and the mansion means it literally: this is enclosed ground, and what is inside is not available for inspection. the difficulty is load-bearing. a structure with one pole is standing because of one thing, and aja ekapāda is a single upright doing the work of a foundation. the classical power given to pūrva bhādrapadā is the fire that raises a person up, with the good of all as its stated basis — so the shelter is not built for one. these degrees hand out the instinct to house other people and no instinct at all for who houses the housekeeper.

born.strike: four stars pitch a small tent in aquarius — saʿd al-akhbiya, the last of the four lucky stations, and the name means the luck of the tents — rendered in the older english lists as the luck of hidden things. the classical sense is seasonal: this is the sky of the moment when the cold breaks and the creatures that had been sheltering come back out of their burrows. so your hunger has two halves. the first is shelter: you are the keeper of safe places — the room people can cry in, the group chat where the bad news gets said first, the friend whose door is a known quantity. the second half is stranger, and it comes from india's name for this sky: pūrva bhādrapadā, whose deity is a one-footed fire-pillar, and whose work is burning off what is false. the same person who makes the safest room in the building also has an incinerator running. you cannot be lied to in your own house. the cost: everyone's shelter, nobody's guest. you have somewhere for everyone to go and no clear answer to where you go.
born.facing: you enter and people exhale. within one meeting they've decided you're somewhere they can put something down. you're read as shelter before you're read as a person.

walkers.name: naila

walkers.name: veth

walkers.name: orna

walkers.name: pell

walkers.name: sarai
walkers.in: sarai keeps a letter she has never opened.

walkers.name: dov
walkers.in: dov guards the way in, which is also the way out.

walkers.name: lys
walkers.in: lys shows you seven tents. she sleeps in the eighth.

walkers.name: the lamp-keeper

claim: the great square of pegasus begins here — the most recognisable four-sided figure in the northern sky, and these degrees are its first wall.
synthesis: a room, an encampment, and the fore-spout of the great bucket that pours the spring rain. india's deity is ahirbudhnya, the serpent of the deep — the coil at the bottom of the foundation, holding it. a wall above and a serpent underneath it.
election: the old books gave these degrees the union of lovers and goodwill, and agrippa — on the mansion of the wall — has them destroying prisons and buildings. the classical indian power assigned here is the bringing of rain, with the growing of plants as its result. every source agrees something comes down.
archetype: a light here builds the enclosure other people will live inside, and the mansion is specific that this is structural work rather than hospitality. markab and scheat are corners, not ornaments. the pairing matters: uttara bhādrapadā is the second half of a pair whose first half is the one-footed pillar, so the sequence runs pole, then wall — and a wall is what makes a shelter into a room. ahirbudhnya is at the bottom of it, in the dark, and the tradition never asks the serpent whether it minds. nobody in a room thinks about the wall, and these degrees do not supply the impulse to mention it.

born.strike: your sun landed on the first wall of the great square of pegasus — four bright stars that make the most obviously built shape in the autumn sky. china saw exactly that and called this station 室, the chamber: a room. the arabs saw the same stars as the fore-spout of an enormous bucket — the lip that the spring rain pours out of. a room, and a spout. both of them are about holding something and then giving it out, and india's name completes the thought: uttara bhādrapadā, whose deity is ahirbudhnya, the serpent of the deep foundation — the thing coiled underneath that makes the structure possible. your hunger is to go still and deep enough to hold weight. you build the room. you are the reason a group has somewhere to be. foundations are under the house. the people enjoying the room are not thinking about what's holding it up, and you will occasionally resent that, and then feel small for resenting it — which is its own second weight.
born.facing: you enter and start building the room — arranging, seating, making sure there's enough. people read you as the host within minutes, whether or not it's your house.

walkers.name: tamir
walkers.in: tamir keeps the gate. your quarter's token goes in his box as you pass, and comes back when you leave, not before.

walkers.name: nasha
walkers.in: nasha keeps the hearth alight all night, because the cot is cold and the room should not be.

walkers.name: vell
walkers.in: vell carries water up from the fore spout. the jar pours whether anyone is lodged here or not.

walkers.name: sadir
walkers.in: sadir mends saddles by lamplight, and every guest's saddle hangs in the bay they slept in. markab is the saddle; this house is named for it.

walkers.name: ennu
walkers.in: ennu cooks for whoever is in, and tonight there is one plate more than there are mouths.

walkers.name: borin
walkers.in: borin walks the hall gate to gate all night and dares it to bring him something.

walkers.name: raqi
walkers.in: raqi keeps the book of guests. she has your name from last time.

walkers.name: the house-watch
walkers.in: the house-watch sits where she can see both gates and the cot between them.

claim: revatī is the last station of india's wheel, and its god is pūṣan — the one who walks travellers to the far side and does not come with them. the arabic name says the same thing about water: the pour completes here.
synthesis: the hind-spout of the bucket, the square's far wall, and a fish. these degrees are where three of the four traditions put an ending that is also a delivery — the last of india's twenty-seven, the closing of the great rain, the far side of the wall.
election: the old books gave these degrees harvests, revenue, and gain, and marked them favourable for marriage. picatrix adds the increase of trade with a caution for sailors, a mixed flag. they also say the stretch hinders building — even guides do not pour foundations.
archetype: a light here takes other people the rest of the way. pūṣan is the god of roads and of lost things and of animals that stray, and his defining quality in the hymns is that he knows the paths and travels them for others' sake. the fish is the same idea in water: something that moves through a medium other creatures cannot. what these degrees withhold is arrival. a guide's work ends at the boundary of the country the traveller wanted, and the one talent this mansion does not confer is knowing what to do once the delivery is made.

born.strike: your sun landed on the far wall of the great square — the second spout of the bucket, the back lip, where the pouring finishes. and india gave this sky the most tender assignment in its entire system: revatī, the last of its twenty-seven stations, ruled by pūṣan — the nourisher, keeper of roads, the god whose specific job is to walk travelers safely home and guide souls on the final road. its emblem is a pair of fish. your hunger is exactly that: you want to see everyone home. the address in the group chat, the text me when you're back, the friend who notices someone left the party alone. you are the last one awake making sure the count is right. the cost is in the job description. a guide walks other people to their doors. you have spent years on the road on behalf of other people's arrivals, and if you sit still long enough to ask where you were going, the honest answer is sometimes that you stopped choosing a destination a while ago because escorting was simpler.
born.facing: you enter checking exits and headcounts, and people feel looked after before they can say why. you are read as gentle immediately and as formidable much later, usually by accident.

card.text: your home cards count one more

walkers.name: teru

walkers.name: isha
walkers.in: isha sounds the depth beside the crossing. she can tell you the number before the pole is wet.

walkers.name: malek
walkers.in: malek carries fill up to the crown all night, so the crown stays a hand above the water.

walkers.name: wen
walkers.in: wen marks the water's height on a post each night. there are a great many marks and this year's is high.

walkers.name: sabra
walkers.in: sabra ferried this crossing before there were stones. her boat is tied up and she would rather it stayed that way.

walkers.name: corvin
walkers.in: corvin opens the culverts so the flood goes under the road instead of over it. it has never once gone over.

walkers.name: dala
walkers.in: dala walks the stones at night with the lantern held low, reading the surface.

walkers.name: the water-watch
walkers.in: the water-watch stands at the middle of the crossing and does not look away from the surface.

synthesis: a fish's belly, a rope, and a stride. the double arabic name is the classic example of layered bedouin sky-imagery — the same stars read as an animal and as a piece of equipment, and both names kept, because neither reading was wrong.
election: journeys, trade, and peace between spouses — the closing works. picatrix has trade, marital peace, and safe travel, and then both books turn: agrippa's twenty-eighth "strengtheneth prisons and causeth loss of treasures." the road ends on a knot, not a bow.
archetype: a light here stands where the road runs out and has not started again. al-rishāʾ is the well-rope, the object that connects two things by being long enough and by being under tension the whole way. china's 奎 kuí is the stride, the gap between one footfall and the next, which is the same fact told as motion instead of rope. what these degrees hand out is the ability to hold two things together across a distance nobody else finds crossable — and the corresponding difficulty, which is that a rope is only doing its job while it is pulled tight from both ends.

born.strike: your sun landed in the last station on the road, and it is the only one that has two arabic names at once: baṭn al-ḥūt, the belly of the fish, and al-rishāʾ, the cord — the well-rope, the tie. the astronomers of that sky could not settle on one image, so both were kept. and there is something here no other station has. the indian sky-map counts twenty-seven stations where ours counts twenty-eight, so this one has no indian name at all. you did not land in a station that four traditions argued over. you landed in the seam between two ways of counting. it is a real feature of the sky, and it is yours. your hunger is the cord's: you want to tie the ends together. you are the person who connects the two groups that should have met, the one who notices that the beginning of one thing is the end of another. and this station's own position says it plainly — it runs right up to 0° aries, where the gate, station one, begins again. you are the knot that closes the wheel and the reason it can start over. the cost of living in a seam: you belong to both sides and are counted by neither. you have been the connector in rooms where nobody thought to count you as a member.
born.facing: you enter and start tying things together — this person to that one, this idea to that project. people meet you and immediately think of someone you should know. you are read as a hub before you are read as a person.

walkers.name: hara
walkers.in: hara turns the windlass. she has never once asked what is on the rope.

walkers.name: tovi
walkers.in: tovi drops a stone and counts. that is how deep you still are.

walkers.name: esk
walkers.in: esk mends buckets. nothing he has patched has ever come up empty.

walkers.name: nira
walkers.in: nira finds water with a bent rod and no explanation.

walkers.name: bel
walkers.in: bel inspects the rope hand over hand, and knows every splice by feel.

walkers.name: kesh
walkers.in: kesh went down once and came back changed. he will not say what he saw.

walkers.name: aven
walkers.in: aven keeps the ladder nobody uses.

walkers.name: the well-watch
walkers.in: the well-watch has looked into the mouth for as long as there has been a mouth.
